Certificate-only and permission-only profile witnesses are recognized by the existing declared profile catalogue.

Absent known optional browser databases are omitted across all 15 families/categories after verified nonlinked component checks. Missing/unavailable profile roots, redirected paths, inaccessible files and unsupported existing schemas remain partial.

Shared bounded recursive discovery covers databases, IndexedDB and WebStorage; explicit Local Storage/leveldb LOCK remains nonrecursive. Optional absence stays empty; links/access/cancellation/limits remain explicit.

Early metadata and Super matches precede full-path StorageDBs, then WebStorage PathDelete, then eligible LOCK keys. Nested Extension Cookies follows its later descriptor and cannot override earlier file owners. No LOCK is claimed by both key and file owners.

Windows case aliases of LOCK/CURRENT/MANIFEST resolve to one observed key-store namespace; ambiguous aliases are refused. Numeric log/table parsing remains case-sensitive: an independent reader ignores uppercase .LOG and refuses missing live uppercase tables, so Rust does not canonicalize those suffixes.

Recursive key cleanup/confirmed restore retains the actual store directory in durable intents, holds every ancestor against replacement and preserves unselected keys and other stores. Legacy intents without the optional directory still bind the original Local Storage scope.

WebStorage file candidates expose observed file units/bytes separately from logical complete review groups. Reviewed file cleanup uses the existing durable journal/Trash path, preserves unselected groups and leaves directories.
Nested WebStorage origin stores bind their own matching origin instead of a shared bucket; unrelated siblings do not invalidate otherwise complete groups.
Recovery uses generic site-storage labels for keys found outside Local Storage. Switches retain the user-requested no-hover styling.

Direct declared cookie files are included in file-owner discovery; SQL adapters skip a direct target when an earlier file descriptor claims it. Early cookies/Quota metadata keeps its earlier SQL priority.
Single-file FileKeys bind the exact reviewed file rather than requiring unrelated profile-directory membership. Extension Cookies refuses file cleanup while any SQLite WAL/SHM/journal sidecar exists.

SQL cleanup checks current file ownership during plan building, before journaling/backup and at existing database access guards. Legacy SQL recovery items are unavailable when an earlier file rule now owns their source.

Successful no-link root validation supplies a canonical profile root before same-family deduplication and scanning. Slash/drive-prefix aliases count once and produce cleanup-compatible native paths; invalid roots keep their existing refusal path.
Named containment and component extraction use the same Windows path identity, so legacy prefix aliases cannot bypass direct file ownership.

Generated Rust constants preserve the declared profile-relative directories, filename masks, recursion flags and complete descriptor order. Other handlers keep their ownership; a fully unmatched nonempty list has no delete fallback.

OriginToDomain.algorithm: Case-sensitive substring search for http_, otherwise https_; if absent return empty. Remove all occurrences of chosen marker and all _0 substrings. Does not parse URL authorities, schemes, ports, percent encodings or public suffixes.

ReverseSuperCookie.algorithm: If .: exists, reverse UTF-16 code units of prefix before first marker. Otherwise reverse entire text and return substring after its first dot, or empty if absent.

Normalizer.algorithm: On nonempty input, case-sensitive find Cookie: anywhere and if found discard first7 units; then find #HttpOnly_ anywhere and if found discard first10. Remove one final slash; remove through first @; remove one initial dot; remove all DOMStore:http:// then DOMStore:https:// substrings; apply CRT towlower per UTF-16 unit. ASCII replay only; malformed prefix-only edge behavior left unknown.

application.order: Read SELECT column0, apply descriptor flag transform, normalize label, then label nonempty/exclusion gate. Read separate raw column1; require nonempty. Each accepted SELECT row increments count; mode-one cleanup uses raw column1 values, without applying label transforms to cleanup keys.

implemented_behavior: Windows PathMatchSpecW matches the exact six Chromium full-path patterns and one Mozilla pattern. Earlier metadata basenames and unsupported Super names retain precedence, with named SQL sources routed to existing row owners rather than whole-file deletion.

Chromium databases/IndexedDB roots recurse. Mozilla cookie variables name containers; typed BrowserProfile consumes their child-profile wildcard, so IndexedDB and storage roots are relative to the individual profile. Recursive named metadata is scanned within that profile. Exact native expansion of unusual/deep/container-root configurations remains open.

Discovery witnesses traverse declared storage roots only, avoiding promotion of Profiles containers or premature exhaustion of the recursive profile-depth budget. Equivalent normal/verbatim drive spellings deduplicate file candidates.

Site extraction preserves first http_/otherwise https_ and last _0 in the full copied path, including unsigned-clamp behavior. Empty native labels do not count; saved DNS keeps omit candidates; unsupported raw labels stay visible but unavailable. Native keep-pattern list sourcing is a separate unknown.

Matching enumerated files retain metadata candidate counts/bytes even when contents are locked, unreadable or over inspection budget; those groups stay visible, partial and unavailable for cleanup. Effect authority requires read-only native identity, single-link and full-content snapshots with pre/post path checks. The whole-file observer introduces no source mutation or file-age threshold.

Chromium payload files from one origin are one reviewed group with separate per-file candidate units/bytes. Initial group membership and every member fingerprint are revalidated before the first effect; files are independently revalidated and browser/policy guards run at each bounded Trash batch. No authority extends to new or differently owned files.

Whole-file and SQL locators are distinct private variants. Exact current review IDs build plans; duplicate/overlapping file capabilities are rejected. Metadata stays with SQL backups/transactions, files with durable generic cleanup journals and recoverable operating-system Trash.

A logical file group succeeds only after every member has a confirmed per-file outcome. Partial native batches preserve uncertainty and never retry; per-file history retains confirmed prefixes. Candidate counts are never treated as successful receipts.

limits.semantics: Limits, inaccessible paths, redirects, hard links, source drift and cancellation remain explicit. No whole-origin transactional guarantee is claimed for multiple recoverable Trash batches.

implemented_behavior: Private reviews bind exact current IDs, complete raw keys, value hashes, normalized saved-keep snapshot and shared source file identities/content. Public records retain sanitized sites and unknown byte totals. Compatible Windows keys become individually reviewable; unsupported sites/platforms or unavailable source guards stay disabled.

The decoder exposes the recovered sequence high watermark, including tombstones and empty-batch recovery semantics, and canonical current/previous log selection. Appends encode full raw-key tombstones at the existing physical log offset with CRC32C/fragment framing, including the seven-byte zero-FIRST boundary case.

Before any source writer opens, exact original selected key/value pairs and immutable source guards are durably backed up, and their digest and operation binding are synced to a separate LevelDB journal. Snapshot and keep/browser checks repeat after intent and before the append.

The existing LOCK is opened without creation, acquired nonblocking, and retained with directory/file handles denying replacement/concurrent writers. Production source writer call sites follow durable intent. Held content/namespace checks and the native lease remain through post-write verification and receipt.

One bounded append batch changes only selected full keys. Planned and actual post-images are decoded and compared with every unselected value preserved. Only verified confirmed removals count as deleted; pre-effect refusal counts as skipped. Partial I/O, post-effect errors or failed durable receipts remain uncertain, retain backups and never retry automatically.

Cleanup reserves log/aggregate-content and sequence capacity for its exact compensating PUT batch before changing source data. Confirmed restore revalidates durable intent, every source file/content identity and fresh reviewed post-state; saves the current log and restore intent; then appends only original removed key/value pairs and verifies all keys. Changed backups, browser restart, new source values and repeated restore refuse.

Existing privacy cleanup, recovery-list/preflight/restore and receipt APIs route the new owner separately from SQLite backups and Trash. Mixed valid/unavailable key selection and restore review reuse existing controls, palette/type and padded dialog frame. No LOCK, SST, manifest, database directory or unselected key is deleted.

validation.initial_linker_output_failures: Two terminal LNK1104 attempts affected absent test outputs; no matching processes and ample space were confirmed before retry. Final full suite and build passed.

implemented_behavior: Shared bounded recursive discovery covers databases, IndexedDB and WebStorage; explicit Local Storage/leveldb LOCK remains nonrecursive. Optional absence stays empty; links/access/cancellation/limits remain explicit.

Early metadata and Super matches precede full-path StorageDBs, then WebStorage PathDelete, then eligible LOCK keys. Nested Extension Cookies follows its later descriptor and cannot override earlier file owners. No LOCK is claimed by both key and file owners.

Windows case aliases of LOCK/CURRENT/MANIFEST resolve to one observed key-store namespace; ambiguous aliases are refused. Numeric log/table parsing remains case-sensitive: an independent reader ignores uppercase .LOG and refuses missing live uppercase tables, so Rust does not canonicalize those suffixes.

Recursive key cleanup/confirmed restore retains the actual store directory in durable intents, holds every ancestor against replacement and preserves unselected keys and other stores. Legacy intents without the optional directory still bind the original Local Storage scope.

WebStorage file candidates expose observed file units/bytes separately from logical complete review groups. Reviewed file cleanup uses the existing durable journal/Trash path, preserves unselected groups and leaves directories.
Nested WebStorage origin stores bind their own matching origin instead of a shared bucket; unrelated siblings do not invalidate otherwise complete groups.
Recovery uses generic site-storage labels for keys found outside Local Storage. Switches retain the user-requested no-hover styling.
meaningful_fixtures: All thirteen families, fresh files, read-only bytes/timestamps, Unicode/nesting, fallback-only profile witnesses, no parent promotion, and optional absence.
Earlier full-path WebStorage origin ownership versus eligible extension keys; early metadata versus late Extension Cookies, directory LOCK, nonrecursive explicit root, count/path/depth/cancel limits.
Windows filename aliases, owned junction refusal and hardlinked input refusal.
Recursive exact-key cleanup/restore, unchanged sibling stores, held intermediate ancestors, stale moved IDs, legacy intent scope and outside/earlier-owner refusal.
WebStorage LOCK counts as a file, complete group cleanup preserves unselected groups/directories, and nonempty keeps refuse generic cleanup.

Generic PathDelete files cannot be matched to kept domains, so any kept-site settings block their cleanup.
Windows exact-key mutations require backups, held identities, post-verification and receipts; uncertain writes retain recovery data without retry.
remaining: Complete global native exclusion/age/access/secure-delete flags and malformed/fork behavior; direct named targets when unusual profile ancestors themselves match full-path descriptors.

Other unimplemented browser handlers, complete native count/byte/GUI aggregation, original/installed and Mac acceptance.

implemented_behavior: Direct declared cookie files are included in file-owner discovery; SQL adapters skip a direct target when an earlier file descriptor claims it. Early cookies/Quota metadata keeps its earlier SQL priority.
Single-file FileKeys bind the exact reviewed file rather than requiring unrelated profile-directory membership. Extension Cookies refuses file cleanup while any SQLite WAL/SHM/journal sidecar exists.

SQL cleanup checks current file ownership during plan building, before journaling/backup and at existing database access guards. Legacy SQL recovery items are unavailable when an earlier file rule now owns their source.

Successful no-link root validation supplies a canonical profile root before same-family deduplication and scanning. Slash/drive-prefix aliases count once and produce cleanup-compatible native paths; invalid roots keep their existing refusal path.
Named containment and component extraction use the same Windows path identity, so legacy prefix aliases cannot bypass direct file ownership.
meaningful_fixtures: Thirteen families times four ancestor layouts: early Cookies remains two SQL rows while Extension Cookies remains two SQL rows or becomes one file candidate, without scanning or changing bytes/timestamps twice.
Reviewed direct file cleanup preserves unrelated profile members and early cookie rows.
Sidecars, cancellation and direct-entry path/count bounds refuse authority.
A stale SQL plan for a file-owned target is rejected before creating an app-data journal or touching Trash; legacy SQL restore listing/review also refuses current file ownership.
Canonical, forward-slash and extended-drive profile aliases yield one physical target and one successful reviewed move.
